tagline: Across Nevada's basins and ranges, with a town now and then.
intro: East of Fallon the highway narrows to two lanes and sets out across the Basin and Range, wide desert valleys broken by mountain ranges. Between Fallon and Delta, Utah, 409 miles off, there are three small towns, Austin, Eureka and Ely. Past Ely the road tops Connors Pass at 7,729 feet, its highest point in Nevada, before it crosses into Utah.

As far as Ely it keeps to the old corridor of the Pony Express and the Lincoln Highway. Life magazine called it the loneliest road in America in July 1986 and did not mean it kindly. White Pine County took the name and ran with it, and the state put up Highway 50 markers of its own.

moments.title: Sand Mountain
moments.text: Some 20 miles out of Fallon the road passes a singing dune two miles long and 600 feet high, sand left behind by the ancient Lake Lahontan.

moments.title: Austin
moments.text: In 1864 this silver town on the slopes of the Toiyabe Range raised over $250,000 for wounded Civil War soldiers by auctioning one sack of flour again and again.

moments.title: Hickison Summit
moments.text: At 6,500 feet a half-mile trail by the highway leads past panels of petroglyphs left by the prehistoric people who lived near the summit.
